title: Sodium-ion battery energy density ceiling
bottleneck: Sodium-ion cells work and are cheap, but their energy density lags lithium-ion by 20-40 percent because sodium ions are larger and heavier and suitable cathode frameworks operate at lower voltages. Hard-carbon anodes — the standard — have sloping voltage profiles that waste usable capacity, and no sodium cathode has yet combined high voltage, high capacity, and long life.
why_it_blocks: Sodium-ion is the great hope for decoupling grid storage from lithium supply crunches. The density gap confines it to stationary storage and short-range vehicles, leaving lithium demand — and its price volatility — undiminished where energy density matters most.
current_state: Commercial sodium-ion cells around 140-160 Wh/kg are shipping for storage and two-wheelers, with steady incremental gains. Closing the gap to lithium iron phosphate levels would require a cathode breakthrough that has not yet materialized.
